1-15231-2-1.subevent: At least four civilians were killed and 10 others were wounded in a mortar attack in northern Faryab province on Thursday morning, according to local officials.
The incident occurred around 11:00am local time when a mortar round landed in a market in Shareen Tagab district, said provincial police spokesman Abdul Karim Yourish.
Yourish said the mortar was fired by the Taliban to target security forces, but all the victims were civilians shopping at the market.
The Taliban has not commented on the attack.

0-4495-1-1.subevent: Tunisia Youth Impact is using cooking contests to encourage young Tunisian women in rural villages to vote in Tunisia's presidential election.
A cooking contest took place in the rural town of Echamine on Saturday, October 12, the day before the second round of the presidential election.
Wafa Tarhouni, president of Tunisia Youth Impact, explained that the contest is a 'practice vote' in which women compete through their dishes to be elected by diners.
Volunteers from Tunisia Youth Impact replicated real-life voting conditions, including electoral lists, voting booths, and sealed ballot boxes, with ink replaced by a water-and-shampoo mixture.

The contest was held in the concrete courtyard of Hinda Jlass's half-built home, where she prepared couscous and said the event was a way of getting together with other women and that the essential thing is to participate.
Hinda Jlass said she planned to vote on Sunday, which would be only the second time she had voted in her life.
At noon, seven other women from the village joined as competitors, or candidates, in the contest.
Each competitor presented her dish to a group of about fifty electors, including couscous, macaroni, rice, salads, and pastries.
The electors tasted each dish and voted using the same procedure as the presidential election, with volunteers guiding them to avoid invalidating their votes.
Members of the ISIE and EU election observer Stefan Ziegler attended; Ziegler said the event was original and could only be a good thing for Tunisian democracy.
After the vote, the ballots were counted, and volunteers pointed out mistakes that could lead to a vote being declared invalid.
Najwa Jlass, the sister of the hostess, won the contest and said she would go to vote 'for real' the next day.

6-18979-2-t.subevent: Crime adapts to society, evolving from individual violations to a differentiated crime structure.
Modern organized crime differs from the past; the Sicilian Cosa Nostra adjusted to a changed economy, shifting its investments from land to real property and businesses.
Organized crime has become networks of alliances across national boundaries, linking the underworld with legitimate institutions and white-collar interests.
Drug trafficking corrupts and kills police and judges, leads users to commit crimes, and launders proceeds into the legal economy.
Organized crime seeks a power monopoly through self-interest, unlike legitimate business, and employs any means without concern for others.
Common criminality and organized crime intersect; thieves pulling a job are not a crime enterprise, whereas organized crime involves continuity, hierarchy, and complex operations.
Organized crime develops a mythology of invincibility used to intimidate, affecting how mafiosi and the public perceive criminal groups.
The complexity of organized crime makes definition difficult; informants' confessions have provided documentation from inside criminal organizations.
Nigerian organized crime is described as having three structural types: pyramidal hierarchy, clan-type networks, and independent cells.

The DOJ stated that Nigerian criminal groups are more pervasive globally than those of any other nation, with the US and Britain as primary targets and heroin trafficking second in volume only to the Chinese.
In 1999, US victims reported several hundred million dollars in losses to Nigerian advance-fee frauds.
In 1997, Boston authorities arrested a Nigerian check theft ring that had stolen over two billion dollars.

0-4931-1-4.subevent: Sheriff Principal Craig Turnbull said the tragedy happened because Captain David Traill ignored five fuel warnings, a 'conscious decision' with 'fatal consequences.'
The police helicopter crashed into the roof of the Clutha bar at 22:22 on 29 November 2013, killing 10 people and injuring 31.

Ian O'Prey, father of victim Mark O'Prey, said he was 'really angry' and that Capt Traill had been made 'a fall guy,' while Clutha owner Alan Crossan expressed 'shock and disappointment' at the report.
During the fatal accident inquiry, Sheriff Turnbull heard testimony from families, experts and eyewitnesses.

In his findings, Sheriff Turnbull said there was 'no doubt' the crash happened because the helicopter's engines 'flamed out' due to lack of fuel, as Capt Traill failed to ensure that at least one fuel transfer pump switch was on.

Sheriff Turnbull said Capt Traill ignored the low fuel warnings and took a chance that they were erroneous, adding that the Pilot's Checklist stipulated he should land within 10 minutes of a fuel warning.
Sheriff Turnbull described Capt Traill's failure as 'inexplicable' and said the Eurocopter EC135 should have had a visible and audible warning when both fuel transfer pumps were switched off.

Sheriff Turnbull said the circumstances were so unusual that they were improbable to be repeated, that the tragedy changed forever the lives of many people, and praised the dignity of those who attended the 32-day inquiry.

Sheriff Turnbull noted it was 'surprising' that it took two years from the 2015 AAIB report to confirm no criminal proceedings, said it took too long to lodge a notice of inquiry, and said the Crown Office's Helicopter Incidents Investigation Team was not sufficiently resourced.
A Crown Office spokesperson acknowledged the time taken was longer than desirable and compounded distress, and said additional funding had been made available.
An Airbus Helicopters spokesman said the company was 'deeply saddened' and had taken immediate action to understand the root cause.

The article's timeline lists key events: the crash, AAIB reports in December 2013, February 2014 and October 2015, and the fatal accident inquiry announced in November 2017 and beginning in April 2019.

3-17441-15-t.subevent: Italy's Economy Minister Roberto Gualtieri said on Wednesday that the main business lobby's forecast of a 6% fall in gross domestic product this year due to the coronavirus crisis is realistic.
On Tuesday national business association Confindustria said the outbreak would cause a serious recession in 2020.
Gualtieri told newspaper Il Fatto Quotidiano in an interview that the estimates are realistic and the Italian economy can aim at a vigorous rebound.
The government is not due to give its own estimates of the impact on the economy until the end of April, when it is scheduled to publish its Document of Economy and Finance (DEF).
Italy's output rose 0.3% last year, and the government expected it to grow 0.6% this year before the infectious disease emerged in the country at the end of February.
At the end of March, two sources told Reuters that the Treasury expected the economy to contract around 3% this year.
Gualtieri said a new stimulus package, set to be approved this month, would be 'significantly larger' than the measures worth 25 billion euros passed in March.
He said it would include an extension of state-backed guarantees for companies seeking liquidity, unemployment benefits and support to people on low incomes.
The minister also said the use of the European Stability Mechanism (ESM) to combat the crisis, under current conditions, was not an option.

He said on top of the European Central Banks' intervention, Europe needed to coordinate a shared fiscal policy and that new solutions are needed to grant parity of conditions and to define an adequate shared and responsible response.
